title: Director of Go-to-Market Engineering (Revenue Operations)
description:
About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including On Running, Breitling, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.


About the Role

We are hiring our first Director of Go-to-Market Engineering.

Perk's revenue organisation is 800 people selling to more than 10,000 companies. Behind them sits a CRM, an enrichment and signal stack, a growing set of AI agents - and a lot of manual work that no longer needs to exist. Your job is to remove it and to build the automated systems that replace it.

You will own GTM Engineering end-to-end: which tools we use, how the architecture fits together, what gets built, and what it does for revenue. You report to the VP of Revenue Operations, lead a small senior team across Europe and North America, and work across SDR, Account Executive, and Account Management - a few high-impact projects each quarter.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it. You will be in Clay, in the orchestration logic, in the agent workflows, building alongside a team doing the same. You're using your experience to guide and coach them to accelerate the pace.

The other half of the job is commercial. The best GTM engineers we have met can sit with a regional Sales VP, work out why their pipeline isn't converting, and leave with the right thing to build. That instinct matters more to us than any single tool on a CV.

What You'll Do

Own the strategy and the stack

  • Define Perk's GTM engineering architecture - how CRM, enrichment, signal, sequencing, orchestration and data layers fit together.

  • Make the tooling calls: what we adopt, what we consolidate, what we retire, and why it pays for itself.

  • Set the roadmap with the VP of Revenue Operations, Sales leadership, and the Revenue Systems and Data teams.

  • Establish the standards the team builds to - version control, documentation, testing, and rollback.

Build, hands-on

  • Design and build in Clay: tables, waterfall enrichment, AI columns, webhooks and API integrations in production.

  • Own the orchestration layer - the logic deciding which records enter a workflow, when, and on what criteria. This is where GTM automation succeeds or fails.

  • Build agentic workflows on modern LLM and agent tooling to take research, qualification, summarisation and data entry off people entirely.

  • Write the code the job needs - Python, SQL, SOQL or TypeScript.

Automate across SDR, AE, and AM

  • Own account prospecting automation globally: TAM sourcing, enrichment, ICP and intent scoring, prioritisation and distribution.

  • Give AEs their selling time back - CRM autofill, quoting, meeting prep, opportunity hygiene, first outbounds.

  • Build account intelligence for Account Management: risk signals, whitespace, account planning.

  • Take each project from prototype to production properly - instrumented and validated before it scales.

Bridge commercial and technical

  • Turn commercial problems into technical architecture, and technical output into impact a revenue VPs recognises.

  • Understand Perk's revenue goals and how to leverage AI capabilities for us to achieve them quicker and more efficiently.

  • Understand and drive clear and tangible commercial outcomes. For example, how to reduce the time that quota-carrying roles spend on non-core activities such as account research, be able to quantify the impact, and clearly communicate the outcomes to leadership.

Build the team

  • Lead and grow a small, senior team across Europe and North America.

  • Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.

  • Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

What Will Make You Successful

Experience

  • Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS

  • Proven track record in GTM Engineering specifically, with delivery at real scale — systems hundreds of sellers relied on, not a pilot for one team

  • Time as both a builder and a leader. This role needs both.

Technical craft

  • Clay expertise in production - complex tables, waterfall enrichment, webhook integrations and AI column logic that revenue teams actually depended on.

  • Deep Salesforce fluency: the data model, integration patterns, and where the constraints really are.

  • Working proficiency in code — Python, SQL, SOQL, TypeScript or equivalent. You pull your own data. Not all coding languages are necessary, but proficiency in one or some is required.

  • Architecture instincts: you build for scale, monitoring and recovery, not just for the first successful run.

  • Depth across several layers of the modern GTM stack - enrichment and data (Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Cognism, PredictLeads), signal and intent (6sense, Bombora, UserGems), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), orchestration (n8n, Make, Workato), data infrastructure (Snowflake, dbt, BigQuery) and LLM and agent tooling. Nobody has all of it. We care that you have real depth somewhere and can learn the rest quickly.

Commercial instinct

  • You judge your work by whether it moved a commercial metric, not by whether it shipped.

  • You have the credibility with Sales leaders to scope the right build - and to say when automation is the wrong answer.

  • You understand the funnel end to end: TAM, ICP, pipeline generation, conversion, expansion, and the economics underneath.

Nice to have

  • Having stood up a GTM engineering function at a high-growth SaaS business, ideally above $100M ARR.

  • Experience taking an automation programme from pilot to global production, including what you learned when it got bumpy.

  • Multi-region GTM experience across EMEA and North America.

Why This Role

GTM Engineering is a discipline being written right now, and most companies are still treating it as a tooling function. This is the chance to own it properly, the stack, the architecture, the build, and the commercial outcome across a $300M+ revenue business with 800 people in the field, a genuine appetite for automation, and the budget and executive backing to move fast.

You would be the first person in this seat, with real systems and real data to work with rather than a blank page, and the freedom to decide what Perk's automation layer should look like. There is a lot to go after, the problems are interesting, and the impact is immediate and visible.

If you want to build the automation layer of a commercial engine at this scale and you want to still have your hands on it come and build it here.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

In this role, you will act as the primary point of contact for our largest hospitality customers across the UK region. You will leverage data, customer feedback, and your SaaS expertise to create value at the enterprise level.

  • Analyze usage data, go-live milestones, and health scores to identify and mitigate risks early

  • Build strong, trusted relationships with C-level and operational stakeholders, positioning Lightspeed as a long-term strategic partner

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Customer Success, Implementation, and Support teams to deliver an excellent customer experience

  • A strong understanding of SaaS metrics (NRR, product adoption, expansion, renewals, churn) and the ability to use them to manage your portfolio

  • A strong sense of ownership; you are hands-on, data-driven, and highly skilled in relationship management

  • Experience managing complex, multi-level stakeholder structures and confidently engaging with C-level, operations, and technical teams

  • Fluent business-level English

  • Experience in the hospitality, POS, or hospitality tech industry is a plus, but not required

 

What’s in it for you?

Come live the Lightspeed Experience…

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you are a driven and focused salesperson with a proven track record of selling cutting edge issuing solutions in a high-growth and competitive environment, this is the role for you. In return, on top of a tremendous working environment, we offer you an unrivalled uncapped recurring commissions plan.

Reporting to the Director, the Senior Sales Manager will handle multiple sales cycles, always ensuring a high conversion rate and outperforming the sales targets.

  • Consultative Expert: Help prospects evaluate Checkout.com, handling detailed questions about our product capabilities, serving as a consultant and industry expert.

  • Proposal Management: Prepare thorough presentations and proposals that highlight the ROI of switching to a modern issuer.

  • Full Cycle Orchestration: Lead the entire Sales process, acting as the main point of contact for clients and internal stakeholders.

  • Collaboration: Partner with other Sales team members to share best practices, key business insights and industry trends

  • Market Intelligence: Provide feedback on local trends including competitor insights, customer needs, sales, product and marketing information

  • Technical Passion: Tech-savvy with a passion for how technology is transforming finance.

  • Business Acumen: Solid understanding of financial factors, including interchange mechanics and card scheme products.

  • Soft Skills: Exceptional communication and negotiation techniques, with the ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder deals.

  • Tools: Knowledge of Salesforce and a highly organized approach to prioritizing shifting workloads.

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We are looking for a Research Engineer to join the research team at ElevenLabs, focused on the data infrastructure that powers our frontier AI models. The quality of our models is bounded by the quality and scale of the data behind them, and you will own the systems that make world-class data possible. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy:

 

  • Building large-scale data pipelines for collecting, processing, filtering, and transforming datasets used to train state-of-the-art models.

  • Training models used in our data processing pipelines, such as classifiers, quality filters, and labeling models.

  • Designing data curation strategies such as deduplication, quality scoring, labeling, and augmentation that measurably improve model performance.

  • Creating tooling and infrastructure that lets researchers explore and train on massive datasets quickly and reliably.

 

Requirements

We do not require any formal certifications or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or GitHub contributions. Ideally, you bring:

 

  • Experience building data-intensive systems, ideally in support of machine learning training pipelines.

  • Strong engineering skills in distributed data processing at scale (e.g., Kubernetes, or custom pipelines over large datasets).

  • The capacity to autonomously evaluate how data quality, composition, and curation affect model outcomes, and to build the tooling to measure it.

 

Bonus: Experience building or operating web crawlers.

 

Location

This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw.

title: Senior International Sales Recruiter, UK/EMEA
description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

At TRM, we believe the people we hire will determine how far and how fast we can go in our mission to build a safer world for billions of people. That’s why we’re building a Talent team that sees recruiting as a craft and a competitive advantage, people who challenge assumptions, move with urgency, and are energized by building exceptional teams to solve incredibly hard problems. If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.

– Alicia Strait, VP of Talent, TRM Labs

As an International Sales Recruiter, you will be responsible for owning high-priority searches across EMEA and other global markets, with a focus on Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and broader business recruiting. You will partner closely with hiring managers and Talent leadership to define search strategy, map regional talent markets, engage passive candidates, and drive high-quality hiring decisions with speed and precision.

Your success will be measured by the quality, velocity, and business impact of hires across TRM’s international business functions.

The impact you will have:

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for international business roles across Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and other functions.

  • Act as a strategic talent partner to hiring managers, advising on market dynamics, candidate calibration, sourcing strategy, and closing approach.

  • Build and execute targeted sourcing strategies that identify, engage, and close exceptional talent across EMEA and other global markets.

  • Develop regional talent maps across priority markets, including high-performing companies, competitor talent, referral-driven networks, and specialized candidate communities.

  • Create an exceptional candidate experience, ensuring every touchpoint reflects TRM’s talent bar, mission, and operating principles.

  • Use data, market insights, and funnel conversion metrics to diagnose search health, influence hiring teams, and refine recruiting strategy in real time.

  • Drive urgency and decision quality across searches by facilitating clear calibration, structured feedback, and timely hiring decisions.

  • Continuously improve international recruiting processes, including intake quality, scorecard alignment, sourcing strategy, debrief rigor, and offer execution.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Talent, People, Finance, Legal, and business leaders to navigate international hiring considerations and keep searches moving efficiently.

What we’re looking for:

  • 5+ years of recruiting experience, with strong experience supporting international business hiring in high-growth technology companies.

  • Proven success hiring across Sales, Post-Sales, Compliance, Marketing, and other business functions.

  • Strong knowledge of EMEA talent markets, with the ability to adapt search strategy by region, function, and candidate profile.

  • Strong search fundamentals, including market mapping, talent intelligence, passive candidate engagement, candidate assessment, and closing.

  • Ability to quickly understand complex business roles across GTM, compliance, marketing, operations, and other functions.

  • Strong analytical ability to interpret recruiting metrics, funnel health, conversion rates, market data, and candidate pipeline quality, then translate insights into actionable recommendations.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trust, influence hiring managers, push back thoughtfully, and operate as a strategic advisor throughout the hiring process.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize market insights, candidate tradeoffs, and search progress clearly for stakeholders.

  • High ownership, persistence, and judgment in navigating ambiguous, specialized, and business-critical searches.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a remote, globally distributed environment with strong overlap across EMEA and U.S. business hours.

About the Team:

  • Our talent team is fully remote, embracing async communication and collaboration through Slack channels, thorough documentation, and proactive updates to keep work moving forward smoothly across time zones.

  • We’re committed to structured alignment, holding weekly hiring syncs for each role, weekly team sourcing syncs, and bi-weekly team meetings to ensure everyone is on the same page and to solve challenges collectively.

  • Driven by a dedication to our craft, we continuously refine our best practices and data quality to deliver an exceptional experience for both internal stakeholders and candidates, supported by precise, reliable reporting.

  • As a globally distributed team, we operate across various time zones, yet most of us overlap for collaboration and meetings between 7am-12pm PST, bringing flexibility and resilience to our work routines.

  • All team members, regardless of location, maintain at least a 4-hour overlap with PST business hours to enable real-time collaboration and drive solutions effectively across the team.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within 72 hours of a role opening, you've scheduled the intake, researched and published the role, and brought 5 calibration profiles to the intake for the hiring manager to review.

  • Within a week of opening the role, you've mapped the total addressable market, built a shortlist of the top 30 profiles, conducted 5–10 recruiter screens, and stood up the full interview process — including the approved questions that define what good looks like on a recruiter screen.

  • Two weeks after the initial interviews, you analyze the data to identify what is and isn't driving pass rates and conversions, share insights and recommendations with the hiring team, and continue to monitor and adjust until the position is filled.

Our Onboarding Process:

  • Within your first 30 days, you’ll be fully onboarded, calibrated, and operating as the DRI for your positions.

  • Within your first 60 days, you’ll have your first sourced candidates reaching final rounds.

  • Within your first 90 days, you’ll have made 2–3 hires.

The following represents the estimated range of compensation for this role:

  • Individual pay is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. The compensation details listed in this posting reflect the US base salary only

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $153,000 - $172,000.

  • Additionally, this role may be eligible to participate in TRM’s equity plan.

  • Please note – we factor in the different costs for geographies outside the United States.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered.

What to Expect From Our Interview Process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Typically 3–5 interviews to go deeper on your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact.

  • Offer: If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions.

  • Welcome to TRM: Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding.

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

Learn more about interviewing at TRM

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate

  • Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more: Interviewing at TRM: How We Hire and What Success Looks Like

 

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Join us in shaping the experience that millions of customers land on every time they open DoorDash, Wolt, or Deliveroo. As part of our Core Consumer organisation, our Homepage team owns one of the single biggest levers we have on what customers find and one of the hardest surfaces in the app to get right.

Working at the intersection of ranking, personalisation, and AI/ML, you'll help decide what each customer sees and why, across three brands and dozens of markets. You'll be building on a global stack, and your roadmap will be a mix: global platform problems that apply worldwide, global capabilities we're accelerating into EMEA, and EMEA-specific problems worth solving properly rather than working around.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Homepage team. In this role, you'll shape how customers discover restaurants, grocery and retail venues, dishes and products — and help define what discovery looks like as AI-driven and agentic experiences change the way people decide what to order.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll be joining a team working on one of the most-used surfaces in the app.

Here's what your day-to-day might look like:

  • Building new end-to-end features and user experiences on Homepage that shape how customers discover restaurants, grocery and retail venues, dishes, and products.
  • Working on ranking, personalisation, and AI/ML problems in the Homepage domain, including how we decide what each customer sees and why.
  • Exploring where AI-driven and agentic experiences change the way customers discover what to order.
  • Making discovery work across three brands and many markets, without flattening into one-size-fits-all.

What You'll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate will bring strong product judgment and curiosity to grow into the rest:

  • Proven experience as a Product Manager on consumer-facing products - discovery, homepage, feed, or ranking-driven experiences are especially relevant.
  • You are a product manager more than a feature owner. Someone who finds the customer problems that matter most and makes the case for solving them.
  • You work backwards from the customer problem, and weigh it against what the business needs most right now.
  • You're comfortable holding several business objectives at once and making a call when they pull in different directions.
  • You work well with a wide range of stakeholders and build trust with people whose priorities differ from your own.
  • You think strategically and can move between long-term direction and what we should ship next.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely flexible (this industry is changing fast, AI most of all).
  • You're curious about what AI actually changes for customers, and can tell real value from hype.

Next steps

The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

title: Director, Credit Risk
description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the only unified payments and financial platform for global businesses. Powered by our unique combination of proprietary infrastructure and software, we empower over 250,000 businesses worldwide – including Brex, Navan, Qantas, SHEIN and many more – with fully integrated solutions to manage everything from business accounts, payments, spend management and treasury, to embedded finance at a global scale.

Proudly founded in Melbourne, we have a team of over 2,300 of the brightest and most innovative people in tech across 27 offices around the globe. Valued at US$11 billion and backed by world-leading investors including T. Rowe Price, Visa, Mastercard, Robinhood Ventures, Sequoia, Salesforce Ventures, DST Global, and Lone Pine Capital, Airwallex is leading the charge in building the global payments and financial platform of the future. If you’re ready to do the most ambitious work of your career, join us.

 

Attributes We Value

We hire successful builders with founder-like energy who want real impact, accelerated learning, and true ownership. You bring strong role-related expertise and sharp thinking, and you’re motivated by our mission and operating principles. You move fast with good judgment, dig deep with curiosity, and make decisions from first principles, balancing speed and rigor.

You're humble and collaborative; turn zero‑to‑one ideas into real products, and you “get stuff done” end-to-end. You use AI to work smarter and solve problems faster. Here, you’ll tackle complex, high‑visibility problems with exceptional teammates and grow your career as we build the future of global banking. If that sounds like you, let’s build what’s next.

 

About the team
The Credit Risk team is part of Airwallex’s Second Line of Defence and helps the company grow responsibly as a global financial platform.
We work at the intersection of credit, FX, and counterparty risk, partnering closely with Product, Sales, Operations, Treasury, Finance, Engineering, Compliance, and Legal to enable commercial growth while protecting Airwallex from financial loss and excessive risk exposure. This is a team for analytical, commercially minded risk leaders who are energized by building scalable frameworks and practical controls across a fast-moving, multi-currency global network.

What you'll do
As Director, Credit Risk, you will lead Airwallex's global second-line oversight of credit, FX, and counterparty risk. You will set the risk guardrails that allow the business to grow safely across merchant acquiring, charge cards, FX, treasury, settlement, and banking-partner activities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Financial Risk, you will own the global framework, risk appetite, limits, governance, and portfolio oversight for these risk areas. You will provide independent challenge to first-line decisions and act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders across the business.

This role is based in London.

Responsibilities

  • Credit risk framework and risk appetite: Define, implement, and continuously enhance the global second-line credit risk framework, including policies, risk appetite thresholds, limits, escalation protocols, and governance standards across Airwallex’s products and legal entities.

  • Credit portfolio oversight: Oversee credit exposures across merchant acquiring, charge cards, B2B and commercial activities, FX pre-funding, treasury-related exposures, settlement flows, and other relevant products.

  • Underwriting and limit governance: Review and challenge first-line underwriting strategies, customer and merchant risk policies, credit assessments, limit-setting methodologies, and exception processes. Act as a senior escalation point for complex or high-value credit decisions.

  • FX risk oversight: Establish and monitor appropriate second-line guardrails for FX exposures arising from pre-funding, settlement, customer activity, treasury flows, and other multi-currency activities. Challenge controls, limits, escalation triggers, and risk reporting to ensure exposures remain within approved tolerances.

  • Counterparty risk management: Set and oversee counterparty risk standards for banking partners, payment partners, merchants, customers, and other material counterparties. Establish appropriate exposure limits, concentration thresholds, monitoring requirements, and escalation processes.

  • Portfolio monitoring and early warning indicators: Lead proactive monitoring of credit, FX, and counterparty portfolios, including exposure, concentration, delinquency, default, chargeback, loss, settlement, liquidity-of-counterparty, and other relevant risk indicators. Identify emerging trends and escalate material issues before they become systemic.

  • Loss mitigation and remediation: Review and challenge first-line monitoring, collections, collateral, prefunding, reserves, chargeback, and other mitigation strategies. Ensure deteriorating counterparties, customers, merchants, or exposures are identified and addressed promptly.

  • New products and market expansion: Partner with Product, Engineering, Commercial, Treasury, Finance, and Operations to assess and challenge the risk design of new products, features, markets, currencies, and partner arrangements before launch.

  • Risk approvals and governance: Lead or support risk committee decisions, material risk approvals, limit exceptions, breach assessments, and remediation plans. Ensure decisions are documented clearly and aligned with approved risk appetite.

  • Regulatory and partner engagement: Represent Credit Risk during regulatory examinations, internal and external audits, and reviews with banking and strategic partners. Prepare clear, decision-useful materials for senior management, risk committees, and the Board where appropriate.

Who you are
We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory.



Minimum qualifications

  • 10–15 years of progressively senior experience across credit risk, counterparty risk, FX risk, treasury risk, or related financial risk disciplines within banking, payments, fintech, or another highly regulated financial services environment.

  • Deep experience designing, implementing, and governing second-line credit risk frameworks in a complex, multi-jurisdictional organization.

  • Strong understanding of credit risk identification, measurement, underwriting, limit management, monitoring, mitigation, provisioning, loss recognition, and capital implications.

  • Demonstrated experience managing risk across multiple product lines, such as merchant acquiring, commercial or charge cards, B2B lending, payment processing, FX, treasury, settlement, or banking-partner activities.

  • Practical experience overseeing FX and counterparty risk, including exposure measurement, concentration risk, limits, settlement risk, prefunding, collateral or other mitigants, and escalation governance.

  • Proven ability to challenge first-line decisions and communicate clear risk positions to senior executives, commercial leaders, product and operations teams, banking partners, auditors, and regulators.

Preferred qualifications

  • Advanced degree such as an MBA or Master's in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or a related field.

  • Professional certification such as FRM, PRM, CFA, or an equivalent qualification.

  • Experience with automated decisioning engines, credit scoring models, portfolio analytics, or alternative data used in underwriting and monitoring.

  • Familiarity with IFRS 9, expected credit loss methodologies, stress testing, or other relevant prudential and accounting frameworks.

  • Strong data literacy and familiarity with SQL, Python, or similar tools used to analyze portfolio, exposure, and loss trends.

  • Experience working in a regulated payments fintech, digital bank, or financial institution with multiple licenses and banking partnerships.

  • Comfort operating in a high-growth environment with evolving priorities and a bias for practical, scalable execution.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

title: Senior Product Manager, KYB - MoonPay Enterprise
description:
MoonPay Enterprise is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend.

MoonPay Enterprise is the fund layer built for businesses. We power how stablecoins move through real financial operations: enterprises, fintechs, PSPs, wallets, and marketplaces running their treasuries, their cross-border flows, and their stablecoin operations on us. The goal is to make moving real money at scale as predictable as any other piece of financial infrastructure, with the compliance and controls CFOs need to say yes.

AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building the rails that businesses run real money on, for humans and agents. MoonPay ranked #2 in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100, made Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 (Top 25 in Finance), and landed on The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running.


About MoonPay Enterprise

MoonPay Enterprise is one of the more operationally complex products in the stablecoin space: multiple banking providers, multiple payment rails, a growing partner base across two product lines (Orchestration and Issuance), and an active compliance surface across each. MoonPay Enterprise runs B2B, B2B2B, and B2B2C models. Partners integrate our API. Their customers become direct customers of MoonPay Enterprise for compliance purposes.

KYB is the front door. Every partner is a business. Every business customer of every partner clears KYB before a single transaction moves. Today the flow is part automated registry verification, part manual review, with different rules for the US and the rest of the world, and turnaround measured in days. That does not scale to where MoonPay Enterprise is going. KYB has to become a product: measurable, fast, API-first, defensible in front of regulators and banking partners. This is a principal seat. You set the multi-year direction for how businesses enter MoonPay Enterprise, and you own the outcome.

What You'll Own

KYB product strategy & roadmap

  • Business onboarding end-to-end, across every model MoonPay Enterprise runs: partners onboarding onto MoonPay Enterprise, businesses onboarding directly, and business customers onboarding through partners.

  • Platform altitude. KYB decisions ripple into KYC, Travel Rule capture, banking-provider onboarding, and Issuance partner diligence. Connect the surfaces; don't optimise one in isolation.

  • MoonPay Enterprise runs three KYC delivery models (reliance, outsourcing, hosted). KYB coverage is uneven across them. You decide where it expands and in what order.

  • Genuine product depth on MoonPay Enterprise is non-negotiable. Within weeks you talk fluently about KYB outcomes, UBO requirements, virtual account structures, and API behaviour. From being hands-on, not from documentation.

Onboarding funnel & conversion

  • The KYB funnel is yours: pass rate, time-to-verified against a 48-72h target, manual review rate, drop-off per step.

  • Instrument what isn't instrumented. Make approval speed and rejection quality measurable. Then move both.

  • Fix rejection UX. Today a declined business often gets a status without a reason, and the partner escalates to support to find out what is missing. Rejection reasons, retry semantics, and resubmission flows become API surface partners build on.

KYB API & partner experience

  • The KYB API surface: statuses, webhooks, document submission, and the edge cases that make business onboarding hard (sole proprietors, corporate shareholders, one person who is UBO, Director, and Representative at once).

  • Partners integrate KYB in weeks and self-serve their onboarding questions. Every "what is missing for this customer" escalation is a product gap. Close it.

Compliance as product

  • Turn compliance-approved onboarding matrices into product logic. US and non-US differ: control prong versus directors, when ownership documents are required, self-certification options. Partners should never need to read a matrix.

  • EDD triggers, high-risk classification, prohibited industries, Travel Rule capture: you decide how they show up in the product.

  • Compliance is your sparring partner, not a ticket queue. You shape how policy becomes product. They own the policy.

Vendor & provider orchestration

  • The verification stack (SumSub today) and the build-versus-buy calls around it.

  • Cost per verification, automation rate, vendor performance. Know when a second provider, a waterfall, or in-house tooling earns its place.

  • Push automation. Decide where AI-assisted review with a human in the loop replaces manual queues, and prove it does not raise risk.

  • Every new banking provider brings its own onboarding requirements. Keep KYB compatible with every rail without collecting everything from everyone.

Who You Are

  • A principal-level PM with real KYB or KYC depth. You have owned onboarding, identity, verification, or risk as a platform, not a feature.

  • High agency. You do not wait for a mandate, a brief, or perfect data. You find the problem, claim it, and fix it.

  • Full autonomy, zero to one. Hand you an unowned surface and you take it from first principles to shipped. No handover document, no waiting for direction.

  • AI-fluent by default. AI tools are your daily instruments for analysis, prototyping, and drafting. You run your own queries; analysis is not something you request from another team.

  • Compliance is a design constraint, not a blocker. You read a requirements matrix and see API design, funnel steps, and copy.

  • You know your funnel cold: pass rate, time-to-verified, manual review rate, cost per verification.

  • At home in API-first B2B. Your users are partner engineers and the businesses behind them, not consumers.

  • You have run verification vendors (SumSub, Persona, or equivalents) and know when to switch, stack, or build.

  • A multiplier for the product team around you. You raise the bar for how compliance-heavy product work gets scoped, specced, and shipped.

  • Bias to action. Reactive stewardship of an existing flow is not what we are hiring for.

description:
Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

 

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

 

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

 

About the Role

 

We're growing our payroll bureau fast and looking for a Payroll Manager to lead a team of Payroll Specialists, driving accuracy, compliance and client experience across their portfolio. This is a people-management role: you'll coach and develop your team, own escalations, and stay hands-on with payroll when it matters.

You'll also be a driving force behind automation and continuous improvement, using AI to cut manual effort and building best-practice, auditable payroll flows as you go.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of Senior Payroll Specialists, Payroll Specialists and Payroll Assistants, signing off their output before it reaches clients

  • Act as senior point of contact for your team's client payrolls, stepping in hands-on for onboarding or escalations

  • Advise clients directly on legislative and regulatory change, and keep the team compliant with a regular gap analysis

  • Own the team's support ticket queue and drive continuous improvement against KPIs and SLAs

  • Lead incident resolution and root-cause analysis, escalating major issues to the Head of Payroll Bureau

  • Identify and implement AI and automation opportunities, and coach the team to build their own

  • Ensure Tax Year-End processing is accurate and on time, and review the team's BACS payments

 

Requirements

 

  • Proven, hands-on experience as a Payroll Manager, including in bureau/outsourced environments with enterprise clients

  • Strong track record coaching and developing a payroll team, combining technical knowledge with people management

  • Comfortable managing the variability of multiple payrolls across different industries within a bureau

  • Strong background in payroll compliance and audit, with good working knowledge of payroll/HR systems and GL structures

  • Bonus: Republic of Ireland payroll experience, CIPP qualification (or working towards one), demonstrable use of AI to automate payroll work

 

Benefits

 

  • Salary: £70,000 - £80,000

  • Hybrid working - 2+ days/week in our London office (Soho)

  • 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days)

  • Extra day of leave for every year of service

title: Retail Industry Principle
description:
About SINGU

At SINGU, we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business.

 

Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide, supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started.

 

Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus.

 

If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation.

The Opportunity

SINGU provides property and facilities management technology for organisations operating complex, multi-site estates. Retail is a strategically important market for the business, spanning shopping centres, retail parks, high-street portfolios, supermarkets, hospitality and other distributed consumer environments.

We are seeking an experienced retail property, facilities or operations leader to become SINGU's senior market authority for retail and help build a differentiated, commercially successful position in the sector.

The Retail Market Principal will combine deep industry expertise, executive credibility and market leadership with clear commercial accountability. The role will help SINGU determine where it has the strongest right to win, create access to senior decision-makers, originate strategic opportunities, accelerate priority deals and strengthen SINGU's relevance across the retail property and facilities ecosystem.

This is not a conventional sales, pre-sales, product marketing or communications role. It is a senior, market-facing position for someone who understands retail property and operations at practitioner level and can translate that experience, credibility and network into measurable commercial impact.

Success will be measured not simply through market visibility or activity, but through SINGU's ability to create qualified pipeline, win strategic customers, expand existing relationships and establish a repeatable position within priority retail segments.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months, you will have established a clear and credible retail go-to-market strategy, identifying the segments and use cases where SINGU can win disproportionately and building meaningful executive relationships across priority retail accounts.

You will have originated and influenced significant qualified pipeline, contributed demonstrably to both new-logo and expansion revenue, and developed repeatable retail propositions supported by clear customer evidence.

You will also have strengthened SINGU's network of retail customers and advocates, while materially increasing our credibility, relevance and market position within the retail property and facilities sector.

What You Will Own

Retail Market Strategy:

  • Define where SINGU has the strongest right to win across retail.

  • Shape our retail go-to-market strategy, priority segments, use cases and target accounts.

  • Maintain a strong point of view on the operational, regulatory and technology issues shaping retail estates.

  • Translate market insight into clear commercial and product priorities.

Executive Access and Market Development:

  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across retail property, facilities, operations, asset management and transformation.

  • Use your network and industry credibility to create access to strategic prospects and originate new opportunities.

  • Represent SINGU in executive forums, customer meetings, roundtables and selected industry events.

  • Build relationships across the wider retail ecosystem, including advisers, FM providers, managing agents and partners.

Strategic Accounts and Commercial Impact:

  • Work with Sales and Customer Success on a focused portfolio of priority retail accounts.

  • Help uncover strategic priorities, strengthen business cases and improve executive engagement.

  • Support selected opportunities where your involvement can materially increase SINGU's probability of winning.

  • Identify expansion opportunities across customers, countries, sites, modules and use cases.

  • Contribute directly to qualified pipeline and revenue growth, without replacing the accountable salesperson.

Customer and Market Insight:

  • Build a strong community of retail customers, advocates and industry influencers.

  • Bring structured market insight into Product, Product Marketing and Commercial Strategy.

  • Identify repeatable customer needs, emerging opportunities and gaps in SINGU's proposition.

  • Help ensure SINGU invests in problems that customers are willing to pay to solve.

Commercial Accountability:

This is not a conventional quota-carrying role, but it has clear commercial accountability. Performance will be measured against:

  • qualified pipeline originated and materially influenced;

  • revenue contribution from strategic retail opportunities;

  • progression and penetration of priority accounts;

  • executive relationships created within target organisations;

  • development of repeatable retail propositions and use cases;

  • customer advocacy and market influence.

Specific commercial targets will be agreed annually.

What We're Looking For:

  • Significant senior experience in retail property, facilities management, estates, operations or asset management.

  • First-hand understanding of complex, multi-site retail estates.

  • Strong credibility and an established network with senior retail stakeholders.

  • Evidence of turning industry relationships and insight into commercial opportunities or strategic outcomes.

  • Strong commercial judgement and the ability to connect operational challenges to financial value, risk and business outcomes.

  • Executive presence, strong communication skills and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively.

  • The ability to identify what is genuinely scalable and commercially valuable, rather than simply interesting.

  • Experience in software or technology is helpful but not essential; deep retail credibility and commercial instinct matter more.

  • Business-fluent English; Polish and/or German language is an advantage

Package and Progression:

  • Competitive base salary, calibrated to experience and location.

  • Performance-related bonus linked to strategic-account engagement, market influence and measurable commercial contribution.

  • Direct sponsorship from the CRO and access to SINGU's executive leadership.

  • Support from Sales, Marketing, Product Marketing, Product and Pre-Sales.

  • The opportunity to shape SINGU's retail market position across Europe.

  • Progression into broader market leadership, strategic growth or industry-led go-to-market responsibility.

If this role sounds like a good fit, we’d love to hear from you. Apply and help us build technology that supports critical operations every day.

title: Member Experience Training & Quality Coordinator - UK
description:
Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

The Member Experience Training & Quality Coordinator makes the Neko member experience standard real on the ground. You deliver our member experience training to teams across the business, primarily clinic teams and centralised support teams, and you run the quality assurance activity that tells us whether the standard is actually landing in practice.

This is a delivery role at the heart of a live culture change programme. You will facilitate training that shifts mindset, not just process, run experience audits against CARE and the Member First Manifesto, and turn what you see into coaching and improvement. As markets scale, you keep the standard consistent across every site and cohort, and rising over time.

You own the coordination and logistics that keep training and quality assurance running: scheduling sessions and audits, and organising the people, spaces and materials each one needs. You report to the Hospitality Programme Lead and support the wider rollout, so you will also play a hands-on part in projects and launch activity as new clinics and teams come online.

What You’ll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Stage 1 and Stage 2 member experience training delivered consistently to every new clinic cohort in your market, with 30-day reviews showing the mindset shift is landing, not just attendance being logged. (Member First, always)

  • A regular quality assurance rhythm is live: experience audits across clinic and support teams, scored consistently against CARE and the Member First Manifesto, with clear findings shared back to the teams and their leads. (Impact, not activity)

  • Audit insight turned into action: recurring friction points named early and at least two concrete experience improvements implemented with clinic and support leads. (Optimistic truth-seeking)

  • Support team training built out and delivered alongside clinic training, so centralised member support holds the same standard as the clinic floor. (Chase 10X, not 10%)

  • The ongoing learning ecosystem running smoothly, including the monthly AI role play and quiz, with completion tracked and shared with Clinic Leads as a coaching tool, not a performance measure. (Tech-enabled, human-centred)

  • A training and audit calendar owned end to end: sessions scheduled around clinic rotas and cohort timing, facilitators, rooms, materials and joining details arranged, and audits planned on a set cadence so every site and team is covered without gaps. (Impact, not activity)

Minimum Requirements

  • 3+ years in training delivery, learning and development, hospitality, or member and customer experience, ideally in a high-touch service, hospitality, or premium retail environment.

  • A confident facilitator, comfortable leading a room of clinicians and operators and holding attention and energy across a full-day session.

  • Hands-on experience running quality assurance or experience audits, mystery shopping, or service standard reviews, with the ability to score consistently and give feedback that changes behaviour.

  • A sharp eye for service detail and what separates a good experience from an exceptional one, drawn from service design and hospitality thinking rather than process alone.

  • Organised and self-directed, able to run a training and audit calendar across multiple sites and cohorts without dropping the standard.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the credibility to influence teams and leads who do not report to you.

  • Willingness to travel regularly between clinic sites, and occasionally between markets.

  • Experience supporting a multi-site clinic, hospitality, or retail rollout as it scales.

  • Experience with digital learning tools, an LMS, or AI-enabled training and assessment.

  • Confident with everyday workplace tools, including Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook, to build training materials, track audits and report findings.

Hiring Process

Candidates progress from application and structured screening through thoughtfully designed interviews culminating in a formal offer and final pre-employment checks before joining the team.

Equal Opportunity & Inclusion Statement

Neko Health is committed to inclusive hiring and member-first care. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to request reasonable adjustments to support your application.

Operations Manager - West Midlands Sort Centre
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M), led by deep-tech investors Plural (whose portfolio spans fusion energy and space exploration), Relay is scaling faster than 99.98% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~110 people, more than half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The Opportunity

You will report to the Site Manager/Head of Site and will run shifts at one of our Hybrid Sort Centres (HSCs), leading 50–100+ operatives through high-volume, time-pressured sortation where minutes matter and small deviations cascade into missed deadlines. Each of our HSCs handle over 40 million parcels annually, with our largest site measuring more than 300,000 sq ft.

You will also be accountable for whether the site is measurably better in a month than it is today for each of our key metrics. You are on the floor for your shift, every shift. This is not a project role with occasional site visits and it is not a desk job, the forward work happens along with running the operation.

 

Who will thrive in this role

  • Deliver shift plan end to end people deployment, throughput, quality standards, and health & safety compliance

  • Lead, develop, and performance-manage a frontline team of 50–100+ operatives

  • Build the mechanisms that hold the operation together. Build controls, cadences, metrics, SOPs, change management and own their adoption, not only their design

  • Plan ahead for future shifts; labour, training, and the risks you can see coming before they land

  • Own the end-of-shift handover; what happened, what is at risk, what the next shift needs to know

  • Stay decisive through volume peaks, outages, and labour gaps. Triage, solve the problem at hand quickly, contain the impact, restore flow

  • Present and write clearly whether briefs, escalations, handovers or post-incident reviews. Decisions here get made based off what you wrote

  • Implement changes into a live operation such as introducing robotics, launching new sortation tech or onboarding new clients. We are changing the operations constantly which means you’ll roll change out mid flight and bring your team along the journey.

 

Who you are

  • Scaled something from zero: a site, a market, a process or a program.

  • Managed a physical operation: quick commerce, grocery, e-commerce fulfillment, last mile, 3PL, food production, airport ground handling, rail. Anywhere with a hard cut off and people on the floor.

  • Communicate in both directions and have strong people management skills: you can brief 80 operatives at shift start and take a problem to senior leadership the same day.

  • Built a mechanism that held: a control, a cadence, a metric, a document standard. Something you authored that changed how frontline teams worked.

  • Own numbers rather than report them: you can name a metric you created or redefined, explain why the previous one was wrong, and say what changed afterwards.

  • Understand frontline work: one of these must be true: you have personally led frontline teams; you have worked embedded in and around a frontline population day to day, without the reporting line; or you have been accountable for outcomes delivered by frontline people you did not employ.

You do not need to have worked in parcels, fulfilment, or sortation. Several of our most talented people had not.

 

Backgrounds that translate well

  • Program Manager in a logistics or e-commerce business

  • Operations Excellence and Continuous Improvement

  • Strategy & Operations

  • Transformation manager

  • Launch and Expansion Manager

  • Regional operations manager

We have hired well from corporate operations, from central operations inside large UK retailers and carriers, and from quick commerce and marketplace operators. Consulting backgrounds work where you implemented, not only recommended; we are keen to understand what you who actually rolled it out.

 

Hiring process

Our hiring process is fast.

  • Initial screen (15 min)

  • Hiring Manager conversation (90 min) - 45 min onsite interview immediately followed by a 45 min site tour where you shadow an existing shift manager

  • Final interview (45 min). Decision and offer within 48 hours

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

You will partner closely with FBPs to challenge operational assumptions, extract key variables, and align strategic direction to fuel "The Engine."

  • Enterprise Valuation & Long-Range Planning (LRP): Build and scale corporate three-statement models and integrated multi-year cash flow frameworks explicitly designed to evaluate macro strategic options, support capital structuring, and drive long-term corporate value creation.

  • Multi-Dimensional Portfolio Cost Allocations: Architect and manage the cost allocation framework required to distribute centralised overhead (shared engineering, global data lakes, corporate G&A) down to individual app-level P&Ls to isolate and report true fully loaded unit economics.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

title: Senior Product Data Analyst - Consumer Growth
description:
About the team

SumUp is best known for helping small businesses get paid — our Consumer tribe builds the other half of that story. We make SumUp Consumer, the wallet app that lets everyday consumers pay SumUp merchants with a tap, send money to friends, track their spending and earn loyalty rewards along the way.

As we grow SumUp Consumer across new markets and features, we need sharp, reliable insight into how people discover, adopt and use the product — and how that behaviour translates into sustainable commercial growth. This includes understanding our acquisition funnel, improving activation and conversion, increasing customer value, and reducing churn.

We're looking for a Product Data Analyst to join the Consumer tribe and become the analytical partner for SumUp Consumer. You'll work closely with Product Managers, Designers and Engineers, alongside our Analytics Engineering team, to understand customer behaviour, shape product strategy, and connect product performance to business outcomes.

You'll help answer questions such as:

  • Which acquisition channels and customer segments generate the strongest long-term value?
  • Where do customers drop out of the journey from acquisition to activation?
  • What drives repeat usage, retention and churn?
  • Which product changes improve conversion, customer value or commercial performance?
  • How should we prioritise product investments across markets and customer segments?

If you're motivated by meaningful analytical work, enjoy translating complexity into clarity, and want to see your insights directly influence both product decisions and commercial outcomes, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Analyse customer behaviour and product performance across the full consumer lifecycle — from acquisition and activation through engagement, retention, churn and reactivation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve conversion, customer value and sustainable growth using funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analytics.
  • Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers and Data teams to ensure decisions are grounded in robust analysis, customer insight and commercial understanding.
  • Evaluate the performance of customer segments, markets, channels and product journeys, helping the team understand where growth opportunities and commercial trade-offs exist.
  • Support decisions that improve key business outcomes, such as activation, conversion, repeat usage, retention, churn, customer lifetime value and revenue-related metrics.
  • Conduct exploratory analysis to answer product and business questions, translating complex data into clear, commercially relevant recommendations.
  • Define, monitor and communicate core SumUp Consumer KPIs, covering acquisition, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, churn and customer value.
  • Design, execute and analyse A/B tests and product experiments, assessing both customer impact and commercial impact.
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that stakeholders actively use, proactively surfacing trends, anomalies, performance risks and growth opportunities.
  • Help Product Managers assess the expected impact of opportunities and evaluate whether product investments are delivering the intended customer and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Analytics Engineering to ensure KPI definitions, business logic and product instrumentation are accurate, scalable and trusted.
  • Bring a curious eye to AI and machine learning techniques, including LLM-assisted analysis, to speed up insight generation, customer understanding and product measurement.

You'll be great for this role if…

  • You have strong SQL skills and are comfortable querying, analysing and validating data in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or similar.
  • You have hands-on experience with product analytics techniques such as funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analysis.
  • You understand the commercial drivers of a digital product, including customer acquisition, conversion, activation, retention, churn and customer lifetime value.
  • You can connect customer behaviour and product performance to business outcomes, and use data to identify growth opportunities and inform prioritisation.
  • You've worked on A/B tests or product experiments, with a solid grounding in the statistics behind them.
  • You're proficient in a visualisation tool such as Looker, Tableau or Power BI, with a track record of building dashboards that stakeholders actually use.
  • You can translate ambiguous product or business questions into structured analysis, and explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • You're comfortable assessing trade-offs, challenging assumptions and making recommendations based on evidence.
  • You're curious about how AI and emerging techniques can improve product measurement, experimentation, customer understanding and commercial decision-making.
  • You're comfortable managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders, with strong prioritisation and a proactive communication style.

This role does not support Visa sponsorship and candidates must have the right to work in the UK.
